# Strict Role-Based Dashboard Separation

Implement strict role-based access control and dashboard separation between **Owner** and **Doctor/Veterinarian** users, ensuring complete frontend and backend authorization.

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> To preserve the Owner's sidebar and navigation when they view a doctor's profile to book an appointment, a new `vet-profile.html` file will be created. This file will be a copy of `doctor-profile.html` but tailored strictly for the Owner experience (Owner's sidebar, bottom navigation, and profile links). The original `doctor-profile.html` will be restricted only to Doctors. Please confirm if this approach is acceptable.

## Open Questions

None at this time.

## Proposed Changes

### Frontend Navigation & Authorization
- **Role Detection**: Update `portal-nav.js` to strictly categorize every page into `doctorPages`, `ownerPages`, and `authPages`.
- **Enforced Redirection**: Intercept any unauthenticated or unauthorized access. Doctors trying to access Owner pages will be redirected to `doctor-dashboard.html`. Owners trying to access Doctor pages will be redirected to `owner-dashboard.html`.
- **Navigation Controls**: Ensure global functions `navigateToRoleProfile` and `navigateToRoleHome` consistently direct to the correct role-specific pages.

#### [MODIFY] [portal-nav.js](file:///c:/Users/VICTUS/.gemini/antigravity-ide/scratch/petcare-app/portal-nav.js)

---

### UI & Layout Adjustments
- **vet-profile.html**: Create an Owner-specific doctor profile view that retains the Owner navigation shell.
- **find-vets.html**: Update the booking links to point to the new `vet-profile.html` instead of `doctor-profile.html`.
- **appointments.html & live-chat.html**: Verify and correct any cross-role link bleeds.

#### [NEW] [vet-profile.html](file:///c:/Users/VICTUS/.gemini/antigravity-ide/scratch/petcare-app/vet-profile.html)
#### [MODIFY] [find-vets.html](file:///c:/Users/VICTUS/.gemini/antigravity-ide/scratch/petcare-app/find-vets.html)
#### [MODIFY] [appointments.html](file:///c:/Users/VICTUS/.gemini/antigravity-ide/scratch/petcare-app/appointments.html)

---

### Backend API Authorization
- **Middleware Enhancement**: Update authorization middleware to enforce strict role-based access. Since tokens in this demo are prefixed (e.g., `vet_token_...` vs `token_...`), we will use these prefixes to validate roles on the server side.
- **Doctor Endpoints**: Restrict `/api/vets/:id/dashboard`, `/appointments`, `/availability`, and `/earnings` exclusively to authenticated Doctors.
- **Owner Endpoints**: Restrict `/api/pets` (POST, PUT, DELETE) exclusively to authenticated Owners.

#### [MODIFY] [vets.js](file:///c:/Users/VICTUS/.gemini/API/routes/vets.js)
#### [MODIFY] [petRoutes.js](file:///c:/Users/VICTUS/.gemini/API/routes/petRoutes.js)

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Login as an **Owner**, attempt to manually navigate to `doctor-dashboard.html`. Verify it immediately redirects to `owner-dashboard.html`.
2. Login as a **Doctor**, attempt to manually navigate to `owner-dashboard.html` or `my-pets.html`. Verify it immediately redirects to `doctor-dashboard.html`.
3. Verify that an Owner booking a vet correctly routes to `vet-profile.html` without losing the Owner sidebar.
4. Test backend endpoints with mixed tokens to ensure 401/403 Unauthorized responses are correctly returned for cross-role attempts.

ArtifactMetadata.Summary: Walkthrough of strict role-based separation implementation.

args.CodeContent:
# Strict Role-Based Separation Complete

I have fully implemented strict role-based dashboard separation between **Owner** and **Doctor/Veterinarian** roles. The application now features robust frontend and backend authorization to prevent any cross-role navigation or data access.

## Summary of Changes

### 1. Frontend Route Guarding (`portal-nav.js`)
- Re-architected `protectRoutes()` to explicitly map every HTML file to its authorized role category (`doctorPages`, `ownerPages`, and `authPages`).
- The system now redirects users precisely to their designated home (e.g., Doctors to `doctor-dashboard.html`, Owners to `owner-dashboard.html`) if they attempt to access unauthorized pages or access auth pages while already logged in.

### 2. UI Separation & Vet Profile Generation
- **Created `vet-profile.html`**: A tailored version of the doctor profile specifically designed for Owners. This file injects the Owner's sidebar and mobile bottom navigation to preserve the Owner dashboard experience while viewing a doctor's profile.
- **Updated `find-vets.html` and `owner-dashboard.html`**: Replaced all `doctor-profile.html` links with `vet-profile.html`. Owners booking appointments will no longer accidentally inherit the Doctor's layout.

### 3. Backend Authorization Enforcement
- **`API/routes/vets.js`**: Enhanced `verifyDoctorAuth` middleware to strictly validate the presence of the `vet_token_` prefix. This middleware has now been securely applied to all scoped endpoints (`/:id/dashboard`, `/:id/appointments`, `/:id/availability`, `/:id/earnings`).
- **`API/routes/petRoutes.js`**: Created and injected `verifyOwnerAuth` middleware. This restricts the `POST`, `PUT`, and `DELETE` endpoints for pets exclusively to authenticated Owners.

## Verification
You can now test the strict separation by:
1. Logging in as an **Owner** and manually typing `/doctor-dashboard.html` in the URL bar — you will be immediately bounced back to `/owner-dashboard.html`.
2. Accessing the "Find Vets" section as an Owner and clicking a doctor's profile — you will now be securely navigated to `vet-profile.html`, retaining your Owner sidebar.
3. Accessing the protected endpoints directly without the correctly prefixed token will yield a `403 Forbidden` response.

I have investigated the entire Vet Profile flow across the frontend and backend, identified the root causes of the "Veterinarian record not found" and blank profile errors, and implemented the necessary fixes. 

Here is what was broken and how I fixed it:

### 1. The ObjectId Mismatch & CastError (Backend)
**The Bug:** The `/api/vets/:id` route was throwing an invisible `CastError` in Mongoose. When the frontend passed a `VCI-...` string to the API, Mongoose attempted to cast it to an `_id` (ObjectId) which requires a 24-character hex string. This caused the query to crash instantly, immediately jumping to the fallback block and returning a `404 Not Found`.
**The Fix:** I updated `vets.js` to validate the `idParam` using `mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid()`. If it's a valid ObjectId, we query `_id`; otherwise, we exclusively search by `vciNumber`. 

### 2. ID Handling from the Vets List (Frontend)
**The Bug:** In `find-vets.html`, the links to individual profiles were defaulting to `vet-profile.html?vci=VCI-2024-8891` if a real vet in the MongoDB collection was missing a VCI number. This meant clicking on *any* newly registered vet without a VCI number navigated to a single non-existent default ID.
**The Fix:** I updated the grid rendering loop in `find-vets.html` to construct URLs using the vet's true MongoDB `_id` as the primary key (`?id=${v._id}`).

### 3. Complete Dynamic Population
As completed in the prior steps, `vet-profile.html` and `doctor-profile.html` have had all their hardcoded demo/fallback data permanently stripped out. 
- It now reads the `id` from the URL, performs an API `fetch` to `/api/vets/${queryId}`, and dynamically binds the response JSON to the DOM.
- We have dedicated UI states for **Loading...** (with a spinner) and **Vet not found** (graceful error handling) if an invalid ID is passed.
- Name, specialization, clinic, contact info, fees, and experience are fully populated.

<script src="portal-nav.js"></script>
    <script>
        document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', async () => {
            const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
            const rawUser = localStorage.getItem('currentUser');
            let currentUser = rawUser ? JSON.parse(rawUser) : null;
            
            let queryId = params.get('vetId') || params.get('vci') || params.get('id');
            if (!queryId && currentUser && (currentUser.role === 'doctor' || currentUser.role === 'vet' || currentUser.vciNumber)) {
                queryId = currentUser._id || currentUser.id || currentUser.vciNumber;
            }
            if (!queryId) {
                queryId = 'vet_101'; // Fallback demo ID if accessed directly by owner without specific prescription DB
            }

            try {
                const res = await fetch(`http://localhost:5000/api/vets/${queryId}`);
                const json = await res.json();
                
                if (res.ok && json.success && json.data) {
                    const vet = json.data;
                    document.getElementById('docName').textContent = vet.name || 'Unknown Doctor';
                    document.getElementById('docQual').textContent = vet.qualification || 'Veterinary Specialist';
                    document.getElementById('docVci').textContent = `Reg. No: ${vet.vciNumber || 'N/A'}`;
                    document.getElementById('docAddress').textContent = vet.clinicAddress || vet.city || 'Address Not Available';
                    document.getElementById('docPhone').textContent = `Phone: ${vet.phone || vet.clinicPhone || 'N/A'}`;
                    
                    document.getElementById('docSignatureName').textContent = vet.name || 'Unknown Doctor';
                    const initials = vet.name ? vet.name.replace('Dr. ', '') : 'Doctor';
                    document.getElementById('docSignatureText').textContent = initials;
                } else {
                    document.getElementById('docName').textContent = "Doctor Not Found";
                    document.getElementById('docSignatureName').textContent = "Unknown";
                    document.getElementById('docSignatureText').textContent = "";
                }
            } catch(e) {
                console.error("Failed to fetch doctor data for prescription:", e);
                document.getElementById('docName').textContent = "Error Loading Doctor";
            }
        });
    </script>
</body>
</html>

args.CodeContent:
# Doctor APIs Implementation Plan

The goal is to connect `vet-appointments.html`, `vet-availability.html`, and `create-prescription.html` to a functional backend API, removing all static demo data and enabling real data persistence.

## User Review Required

Currently, the backend (`vets.js`) uses a simple in-memory object (`doctorDataStore`) to mock appointments and availability, and it has no concept of prescriptions. 
To build a proper, scalable application, **we should create real MongoDB Collections (Mongoose Models) for Appointments and Prescriptions**. 

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Please confirm if you approve creating MongoDB models for Appointments and Prescriptions**, or if you'd prefer I just extend the temporary in-memory store for quick testing.

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Database Models (Backend)
I will create two new Mongoose schema files to define the data structures:
- #### [NEW] `API/models/Appointment.js`
  Will store fields such as `vetId`, `petId`, `ownerName`, `petName`, `date`, `time`, `status` (e.g. pending, completed, urgent), and `consultationType`.
- #### [NEW] `API/models/Prescription.js`
  Will store fields such as `vetId`, `patientName`, `diagnosis`, `symptoms`, an array of `medications` (name, dosage, frequency), and `instructions`.

### 2. API Endpoints (`API/routes/vets.js`)
I will update and add the following endpoints to interact with MongoDB instead of the in-memory store:
- `GET /api/vets/:id/appointments`: Fetch all appointments for a specific doctor.
- `GET /api/vets/:id/availability`: Fetch the doctor's weekly schedule. (We will store this directly on the `Vet` model).
- `PUT /api/vets/:id/availability`: Update the doctor's weekly schedule.
- `POST /api/vets/:id/prescriptions`: Submit and save a new prescription.

### 3. Frontend Integration
I will modify the three HTML files to consume the new APIs:

#### [MODIFY] `scratch/petcare-app/vet-appointments.html`
- Remove the hardcoded table rows.
- Add a script to fetch `GET /api/vets/:id/appointments` and dynamically render the rows (Patient Name, Time, Status, Actions).

#### [MODIFY] `scratch/petcare-app/vet-availability.html`
- Add a script to fetch the doctor's saved schedule on page load and populate the toggles/time inputs.
- Wire up the "Save Changes" button to construct a JSON payload and send a `PUT` request to the API.

#### [MODIFY] `scratch/petcare-app/create-prescription.html`
- Wire up the "Issue & Send" button.
- Extract the dynamic medication rows, diagnosis, and patient info into a JSON payload.
- Send a `POST` request to the backend to officially record the prescription in the database.

## Verification Plan
1. We will verify that saving availability persists across page refreshes.
2. We will submit a prescription via `create-prescription.html` and verify it saves to the database successfully.
3. We will verify the appointments table loads real data from the API endpoint.

args.CodeContent:
# Doctor Appointments, Availability & Prescriptions API Walkthrough

I have successfully updated the backend API and frontend pages to support Doctor Appointments, Availability, and Prescriptions! 

## Changes Made

### 1. New MongoDB Data Models
- Created `API/models/Appointment.js` to manage the schema for doctor-patient appointments, including fields for pet details, consultation types, and statuses.
- Created `API/models/Prescription.js` to structure the digital prescriptions issued by veterinarians, holding an array of prescribed medications and diagnosis notes.

### 2. Backend API Integration (`vets.js`)
I updated the existing `/api/vets/:id/...` routes to interface with our new models securely:
- **`GET /api/vets/:id/appointments`**: Fetches real appointments associated with the Doctor's ID from MongoDB. 
- **`POST /api/vets/:id/appointments`**: Allows the system to insert new appointments.
- **`GET` & `PUT /api/vets/:id/availability`**: Allows doctors to fetch and update their weekly shift hours and emergency mode toggle.
- **`POST` & `GET /api/vets/:id/prescriptions`**: Allows creating and fetching Rx prescriptions securely assigned to the doctor.

> [!NOTE] 
> The API retains an automatic memory-fallback capability, so if the database server experiences temporary issues, doctors can still load and issue data from their scoped session memory.

### 3. Frontend Dynamic Integration
I removed the static mock data from the HTML templates and integrated standard Javascript `fetch()` operations to connect with the backend APIs:

#### `vet-appointments.html`
- Now clears out the hardcoded queue on load.
- Automatically fetches the list of appointments for the currently logged-in veterinarian from the `/appointments` API.
- Generates HTML table rows dynamically based on the returned payload.

#### `vet-availability.html`
- The "Save Availability Schedule" button now correctly reads the selected shifts (e.g., 09:00 - 17:00), the Emergency Duty toggle, and dispatches a `PUT` request containing a structured JSON object to the API.

#### `create-prescription.html`
- The Rx issuing form was upgraded. Clicking "Save Prescription" now gathers the patient information and prescribed drugs, then executes a `POST` request to securely save the Rx record onto the database before redirecting the doctor to the dashboard.

## Next Steps
You can navigate to your doctor dashboard on `localhost:3000` to test out the new functional appointment listings, save your shift availability, and issue a digital prescription! Let me know if you would like to refine any of the form scraping behaviors or add additional features!
